question.problem:
The equation of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}=108$ in standard form is{{field-1}}
$=1.$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $108$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2} & =108 \\ \frac{9{y}^{2}}{108}-\frac{4{x}^{2}}{108} & =\frac{108}{108} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{12}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{27} & =1\end{aligned}
$$
